title: Engine sub-variant Wang support + grass family rewrite (curved edges, overhang, 3 sub-variants per Wang index) — first consumer of the tile-edge-library pattern
intent: Per `docs/game-design/tile-edge-library-design.md`. User feedback 2026-06-03 (4 rounds): tiles read as cubes, grass islands as squares, edges need to be irregular, same pattern для всех biomes + cliffs. Comprehensive design now in tile-edge-library-design.md. This story scopes the FOUNDATION + GRASS first consumer: (1) extend engine Wang module with sub-variant array support (variants[16][] instead of [16]) + deterministic per-cell sub-variant hash. (2) Replace S176 grass-variants.ts with curved-outline mesh generation — 5 shapes × 4 rotations × 3 sub-variants = 60 distinct meshes generated procedurally. (3) Mesh has 0.18 cells overhang on open edges + Y-axis blade-noise displacement + downward Y-slope at edge curl. (4) Sub-variant cell-hash ensures adjacent grass cells with same Wang bitmask use DIFFERENT meshes (no visible repetition). After this lands, the SAME pattern propagates to path/stone/dirt/cliff via follow-up stories (filed separately by dev). Establishes the architecture; doesn't re-do everything in one sprint.
rationale: Source: 4 rounds of user feedback on tiling consolidated into tile-edge-library-design.md. Engine extension is small (~50 LOC); grass rewrite is the demonstrably-failing case (S176 = flat boxes). Establishing the pattern with grass enables dev to file follow-up stories applying same pattern to other biomes + cliffs without re-deciding architecture. Supersedes GDP-2026-05-29-007 (deferred-and-archived grass spec). Defers GDP-2026-05-30-003 (Wang 2-corner) — overlay architecture replaces multi-primary blending need.
acceptanceHints: READ FIRST: `docs/game-design/tile-edge-library-design.md` — canonical architecture spec (7-layer pipeline, sub-variant pattern, shape table, per-biome interior recipes).
ENGINE EXTENSION — `engine/render/autotile/`:
WangTileFamily.variants schema: extend to allow `variants: WangTileVariant[16] | WangTileVariant[16][]`. Sub-variant arrays per Wang index (each index gets N alternatives).
Resolver picks: variants is single → variants[bitmask]; variants is grouped → variants[bitmask][hash(cellGx, cellGz, sceneSeed) % len].
Hash function: deterministic per (cell, scene seed). Same cell + same scene = same sub-variant on reload.
Backwards-compatible: existing families with [16] keep working.
~50 LOC + tests.
GRASS FAMILY REWRITE — `examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/grass-variants.ts`:
Replaces S176 entirely. Same exported function signature `buildGrassVariant(bitmask, subVariantIdx?)`.
GEOMETRY GENERATION RECIPE (per (bitmask, subVariant) combination):
1. CHOOSE shape from 5 base shapes per tile-edge-library-design.md §6:
Shape A (bitmask 0): round/oval — outline = circle radius 0.6 cells.
Shape B (bitmasks 1/2/4/8): edge — 3 open curved sides + 1 closed flush.
Shape C (bitmasks 3/6/9/12): corner — 2 closed flush + 2 open curved.
Shape D (bitmasks 5/10): straight — 2 parallel open curved + 2 closed flush.
Shape E (bitmasks 7/11/13/14): T-junction — 3 closed flush + 1 open curved.
Shape F (bitmask 15): filler — 1×1 square (no curves).
Rotation applies per S214 lookup.
2. SAMPLE outline polygon — for each curved edge:
Generate 8-12 points along quadratic Bezier sampling.
Control point displacement varies per sub-variant — sub A peaks at (0.18, 0.0), sub B at (0.20, 0.08), sub C two smaller bulges at (0.10, ±0.15).
All sub-variants share connection points to neighbour cells (closed-edge corners stay at cell boundary).
3. EXTEND polygon outward 0.18 cells on open edges — the overhang. Outermost vertex Y → 0.05 (slopes down to floor level).
4. TRIANGULATE the polygon top face — use Three.js ShapeGeometry OR custom mesh builder. Subdivide into ~10×10 vertex grid for blade-noise displacement.
5. APPLY blade-noise Y displacement on top-face vertices — Y += bladeNoise(x, z) ∈ 0..0.06 cells (deterministic seeded hash per vertex).
6. EXTRUDE downward 0.15 cells (top at Y=0.20, bottom at Y=0.05 — overlay sits above floor backdrop at Y=0).
7. SIDE FACES: vertical strips from top polygon to bottom polygon. Use cliff-face-style material variant (darker GRASS_SHADOW tint).
8. VERTEX COLOURS:
Base = GRASS_PRIMARY (#4a8a3e).
Higher-Y vertices blend toward GRASS_HIGHLIGHT (#5fa84a) — bright tips.
Lower-Y vertices blend toward GRASS_SHADOW (#3a6a30) — root shadow.
Theme palette overridable per S172 pattern.
WANG REGISTRATION:
`examples/kaboom-crew/src/blocks/register-wang-families.ts`: re-register 'grass' family with sub-variants:
- bitmasks: 16
- sub-variants per index: 3 (constant for grass)
- builder: (bitmask, subIdx) => buildGrassVariant(bitmask, subIdx)
PERFORMANCE TARGETS:
Mesh cache: 60 distinct meshes (5 shapes × 4 rotations × 3 sub-variants) per grass family. ~12000 cached vertices. ~150KB. Within budget.
Per cell: ~200 vertices avg. At 100 grass cells: 20000 vertices. Fine.
Wang resolver cost: unchanged from S169 (sub-variant lookup adds 1 hash + 1 modulo per cell — negligible).
TESTS:
buildGrassVariant(0, 0) returns mesh with circular outline + > 100 vertices (curved + subdivided).
buildGrassVariant(8, 0) returns mesh with 3 curved sides + 1 straight (N-edge cell-boundary).
buildGrassVariant(0, 0) != buildGrassVariant(0, 1): different control points → different vertex positions (sub-variant works).
buildGrassVariant(0, 0) == buildGrassVariant(0, 0): determinism.
Sub-variant cell selection: cell (5, 5) with scene seed 42 deterministically picks same sub-variant on reload.
Overhang: outline points on open edges extend beyond cell boundary (up to 1.18 × cell-size in open direction).
VISUAL QA (user's actual ask):
Load grass-demo arena → 4×4 grass cluster reads as ONE ORGANIC ISLAND, no perceptible cell-seam boundaries.
Edges visibly curved (not square). Adjacent cells with same Wang bitmask use DIFFERENT sub-variants → no repetition.
Single isolated cell → small round mound.
Long strip → wavy ribbon.
